easy.def: A big tree with wide leaves and bark that peels.
examples: The sycamore is tall.
We sat under the sycamore.
The sycamore has big leaves.

more.def: A large tree with wide leaves and bark that peels off in patches, found beside rivers and streets.
examples: A giant sycamore shaded the whole front yard.
The bark of the sycamore peels off in patches, showing the white wood underneath.
Wide sycamore leaves turned yellow in the fall.

easy.def: A part of a word with one beat.
examples: "Cat" has one syllable.
Clap each syllable.
"Water" has two syllables.

more.def: A part of a word that has one vowel sound and is said in one beat, such as "pen" and "cil" in "pencil."
examples: The word "cat" has one syllable, and "butter" has two.
We clapped once for each syllable in the word.
The stress is on the first syllable of "happy."

easy.def: A picture or sign that stands for something.
examples: A heart is a symbol of love.
A dove is a symbol of peace.
The flag is a symbol.

more.def: A sign, picture or object that stands for an idea or thing.
examples: A red cross is a symbol that shows help is near.
The dove is a symbol of peace.
The plus sign is the symbol for adding.
The dove is symbolic of peace.
A symbolic gift.
A symbolic act.

more.def: Standing for or showing an idea in a way that is not literal.
examples: The white dove is symbolic of peace.
The flag is symbolic of the country.
Giving a ring is a symbolic act of love.
A dove will symbolize peace.
The heart symbolizes love.
The flag symbolizes our country.

more.def: To be a sign of something or stand for an idea.
examples: A white dove symbolizes peace.
The red heart symbolizes love.
Green lights symbolize go on a traffic signal.

easy.def: Feeling sorry for someone who is sad or hurt.
examples: The nurse was sympathetic.
A sympathetic friend listened.
He had a sympathetic look.

more.def: Showing that you care about someone's sadness or trouble.
examples: The nurse was sympathetic when I hurt my knee.
A sympathetic friend listened when I felt sad.
He gave me a sympathetic look and said he was sorry.

easy.def: To feel sorry for someone who is sad.
examples: I sympathize with you.
She sympathized with her friend.
We sympathize.

more.def: To show that you understand and care about how someone else feels, especially when they are sad.
examples: I sympathize with you; I lost a tooth, too, and it hurt.
She sympathized with her friend who had lost the game.
We sympathized with the family whose house flooded.

easy.def: Feeling sorry for someone who has a problem.
examples: I felt sympathy for her.
We sent a card of sympathy.
He showed sympathy.

more.def: A feeling of sorrow for someone who is hurt or sad.
examples: I felt sympathy for my friend who lost her pet.
We sent a card to show our sympathy.
The nurse showed sympathy to the child.

easy.def: A long piece of music for a large group of musicians.
examples: We heard a symphony.
The symphony was long.
She played in the symphony.

more.def: A long piece of music written for a large orchestra, or the orchestra itself.
examples: We heard a symphony by Beethoven at the concert hall.
She plays the violin in the city symphony.
The symphony has four parts, and each one sounds different.

easy.def: A sign that you are sick.
examples: A cough is a symptom of a cold.
A fever is a symptom.
The symptoms went away.

more.def: A sign of an illness that you can feel or see.
examples: A runny nose is a symptom of a cold.
A fever is a common symptom of the flu.
The doctor asked about her symptoms.

easy.def: Made by people, not found in nature.
examples: The jacket is synthetic.
Plastic is synthetic.
This rope is synthetic.

more.def: Made by people from chemicals or other materials, rather than coming from nature.
examples: Nylon is a synthetic cloth made in factories, not from plants or animals.
The toy was made from synthetic rubber.
Her jacket was synthetic, not made of real wool.

easy.def: A tool with a needle that nurses use for shots.
examples: The nurse used a syringe.
A syringe holds medicine.
He saw a syringe.

more.def: A tube with a plunger and often a needle, used by doctors and nurses to give medicine or to take blood.
examples: The nurse filled the syringe with medicine before giving the shot.
A syringe has a plunger that pushes liquid out through the needle.
The vet used a syringe to give the dog a vaccine.
I put syrup on my pancakes.
The syrup is sweet.
Maple syrup is brown.

more.def: A thick, sweet liquid that is poured over food.
examples: I poured syrup on my pancakes.
The syrup was thick and sweet.
Maple syrup comes from tree sap.
The school has a bus system.
Your body has a system for breathing.
A computer system has many parts.

more.def: A set of parts or ideas that work together as a whole.
examples: The subway system carries thousands of people every day.
Your body has a system that carries blood.
Our teacher has a system for handing out papers.
